identity.name: Active Directory Privilege Escalation & Token Manipulation Chain — LSASS to SYSTEM (T1068 / T1134 / T1003.001)
identity.summary: Against the authorised CortexSim AD lab, a post-compromise operator escalates from foothold to SYSTEM: pypykatz parses LSASS, bloodyAD writes an abnormal DACL on a privileged object, KrbRelayUp does a local Kerberos relay, PrintSpoofer abuses SeImpersonate to spawn SYSTEM, and Tokenvator steals a privileged token. Cortex ITDR/XDR fire on each step.
identity.description: This card reproduces the canonical Windows local-to-domain privilege-escalation chain that follows nearly every Active Directory intrusion, executed end-to-end against the deliberately-misconfigured CortexSim AD lab (the `itdr` IaC module: a Server 2022 Domain Controller plus domain-joined workstations seeded with roastable accounts and a DA-equivalent helpdesk-admin). Five dual-use techniques are detonated in sequence. (1) LSASS Memory credential dumping (T1003.001): pypykatz parses a captured LSASS minidump to recover plaintext, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos keys — the upstream tell is a non-system process opening a credential-read handle to lsass.exe. (2) AD DACL abuse / Account Manipulation (T1098): bloodyAD writes an abnormal nTSecurityDescriptor (GenericAll / WriteDACL) onto a privileged group or AdminSDHolder, an ACL-based escalation path that grants the foothold account control over Domain Admins. (3) Kerberos relay local privilege escalation (T1550 / T1068): KrbRelayUp triggers the machine account to authenticate, relays that Kerberos authentication to LDAP, and configures Resource-Based Constrained Delegation against the local computer object to obtain a SYSTEM ticket — a self-relay observable as a Kerberos relay from the local host to LDAP. (4) SeImpersonate abuse (T1134): PrintSpoofer leverages the SeImpersonatePrivilege held by service accounts (IIS, MSSQL) to capture a SYSTEM token over a named pipe and spawn a SYSTEM process — the 'potato' family escalation. (5) Access Token Manipulation / theft (T1134): Tokenvator duplicates and impersonates the access token of a privileged process (e.g. winlogon.exe) so the operator's process runs in that security context. The detection model is identity- and endpoint-behavioural: a BIOC fires on the LSASS credential-access handle from a non-system process; a BIOC fires on the abnormal DACL write to a privileged AD object (4662 directory-service write); a BIOC fires on the local Kerberos relay to LDAP; a BIOC fires on a SeImpersonate service account spawning a SYSTEM child via a named pipe; a BIOC fires on the token-duplication/impersonation from a privileged process. Validation XQL confirms LSASS access, the privileged DACL modification, the SYSTEM child spawned from a service-account parent, and the overall local-to-SYSTEM escalation chain; a correlation rule groups the steps from one host into a single Privilege Escalation incident. The harvested credentials and SYSTEM context become the pivot for the separate lateral-movement and DCSync chains (SIM-MP-002).

data_sources: Active Directory: Active Directory Object Modification

prerequisites.description: Cortex ITDR + XDR connected to the Active Directory domain and the domain-joined workstation (security-event, process, and LDAP/Kerberos telemetry) on the authorised CortexSim AD lab.
Lab matching the `itdr` IaC module: a Server 2022 DC and at least one domain-joined workstation reachable from the jumpbox with a low-privilege foothold account.

Adapter consent (simulation_authorized) granted at launch — the dual-use-lab-only adapters TOOL-PYPYKATZ / TOOL-BLOODYAD / TOOL-KRBRELAYUP / TOOL-PRINTSPOOFER / TOOL-TOKENVATOR are consent-gated by the orchestrator.

payload.code:
# All activity targets the authorised CortexSim itdr-module AD lab.
# 1. LSASS credential parse.
pypykatz lsa minidump /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_lsass.dmp
# 2. Abnormal DACL write on a privileged object.
bloodyAD --host 10.0.10.10 -d cortexsim.local -u 'cortexsim\\helpdesk-admin' -p "$WS_PWD" add genericAll 'CN=Domain Admins,CN=Users,DC=cortexsim,DC=local' 'cortexsim\\helpdesk-admin'
# 3. Kerberos relay local privesc.
KrbRelayUp.exe relay -d cortexsim.local -cls
# 4. SeImpersonate -> SYSTEM.
PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c whoami
# 5. Access token theft / impersonation.
Tokenvator.exe Steal_Token 4 winlogon.exe

input_variables.name: WS_PWD
input_variables.description: Password for the low-privilege foothold account on the authorised CortexSim AD lab.

expected_artifacts.description: A non-system process opens a credential-read handle to lsass.exe (LSASS memory dumping).
A 4662 directory-service object write modifying nTSecurityDescriptor on a privileged group (DACL abuse).
A SYSTEM-integrity child process spawned from a SeImpersonate-holding service-account parent via a named pipe.
A local Kerberos relay from the host to LDAP (KrbRelayUp self-relay).

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-ITDR-007 cleanup — removing simulated escalation artifacts'; rm -f /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_creds.txt /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_dacl.txt /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_krbrelay.txt /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_printspoofer.txt /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_tokenvator.txt /tmp/cortexsim_itdr007_lsass.dmp

biocs.name: ITDR-007 LSASS Process Handle Open By Non-System Process
biocs.description: XDR - a non-system process opens a process handle to lsass.exe with credential-read access rights. Reading LSASS memory is the canonical credential-dumping primitive (T1003.001); pypykatz parses the resulting dump offline.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| filter action_type = ENUM.PROCESS_HANDLE
| filter lower(target_process_image_name) = "lsass.exe"
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM", "NT AUTHORITY\\LOCAL SERVICE")
| filter requested_access_mask contains "0x10"
| fields _time, src_host, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, actor_effective_username, requested_access_mask

biocs.name: ITDR-007 Abnormal DACL Write To AdminSDHolder Or Privileged Group
biocs.description: ITDR - an abnormal write to the nTSecurityDescriptor (DACL) of AdminSDHolder or a privileged group (Domain Admins / Enterprise Admins) granting GenericAll or WriteDACL. ACL-based escalation (T1098) lets a foothold account take control of privileged objects; bloodyAD writes the malicious ACE.
biocs.logic:
dataset = ad_audit
| filter event_id = 4662
| filter lower(object_properties) contains "writedacl" or lower(object_properties) contains "ntsecuritydescriptor"
| filter lower(object_name) contains "adminsdholder" or lower(object_name) contains "domain admins" or lower(object_name) contains "enterprise admins"
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("Administrator", "svc-adsync")
| fields _time, src_host, actor_effective_username, object_name, object_properties

biocs.name: ITDR-007 Kerberos Relay To LDAP From Local Host (KrbRelayUp)
biocs.description: ITDR - a Kerberos authentication is relayed from the local host to LDAP/LDAPS on a domain controller, immediately followed by a write to the local computer object's msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity (RBCD). This self-relay to obtain a SYSTEM ticket is the KrbRelayUp local-privilege-escalation fingerprint (T1550 / T1068).
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter dst_port in (389, 636)
| filter lower(app_id) contains "kerberos" or lower(auth_protocol) contains "kerberos"
| filter src_host = dst_host
| fields _time, src_host, dst_host, dst_port, actor_process_image_name

biocs.name: ITDR-007 SeImpersonate Named-Pipe Privilege Escalation To SYSTEM
biocs.description: XDR - a service account holding SeImpersonatePrivilege (IIS w3wp.exe, MSSQL sqlservr.exe, or a 'potato' tool) spawns a child process running as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM via named-pipe token impersonation. This is the PrintSpoofer / potato-family local escalation (T1134).
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| filter action_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username = "NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM"
| filter lower(causality_actor_process_image_name) in ("w3wp.exe", "sqlservr.exe", "printspoofer64.exe", "printspoofer.exe")
| fields _time, src_host, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, actor_effective_username

biocs.name: ITDR-007 Access Token Theft And Impersonation Via Token Duplication
biocs.description: XDR - a process duplicates and impersonates the access token of a privileged/SYSTEM process (e.g. winlogon.exe) so it runs in that security context. DuplicateTokenEx + ImpersonateLoggedOnUser against a high-privilege parent is the access-token-theft fingerprint (T1134); Tokenvator automates it.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| filter action_type = ENUM.PROCESS_TOKEN
| filter lower(target_process_image_name) in ("winlogon.exe", "lsass.exe", "services.exe")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM")
| fields _time, src_host, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_id, actor_effective_username, target_process_image_name

xql_queries.name: ITDR-007 Validate LSASS Credential Access By Non-System Process
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| filter action_type = ENUM.PROCESS_HANDLE
| filter lower(target_process_image_name) = "lsass.exe"
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM")
| comp count() as lsass_handles by src_host, actor_process_image_name, actor_effective_username
| filter lsass_handles >= 1
| fields src_host, actor_process_image_name, actor_effective_username, lsass_handles

xql_queries.name: ITDR-007 Validate Abnormal Privileged DACL Modification
xql_queries.query:
dataset = ad_audit
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_id = 4662
| filter lower(object_properties) contains "writedacl" or lower(object_properties) contains "ntsecuritydescriptor"
| filter lower(object_name) contains "adminsdholder" or lower(object_name) contains "domain admins" or lower(object_name) contains "enterprise admins"
| comp count() as dacl_writes by src_host, actor_effective_username, object_name
| filter dacl_writes >= 1
| fields src_host, actor_effective_username, object_name, dacl_writes

xql_queries.name: ITDR-007 Validate SYSTEM Token Spawned From Service Account Process
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_id = 4688
| filter lower(new_process_token_user) contains "system"
| filter lower(creator_process_name) in ("w3wp.exe", "sqlservr.exe", "printspoofer64.exe", "printspoofer.exe")
| comp count() as system_spawns by src_host, creator_process_name, new_process_name
| filter system_spawns >= 1
| fields src_host, creator_process_name, new_process_name, system_spawns

xql_queries.name: ITDR-007 Validate Local Privilege Escalation Chain To SYSTEM
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS
| filter action_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username = "NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM"
| filter lower(causality_actor_process_image_name) not in ("services.exe", "wininit.exe", "smss.exe", "system")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as system_children by src_host, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter system_children >= 1
| fields src_host, causality_actor_process_image_name, system_children

correlation_rules.name: AD Local-to-SYSTEM Privilege Escalation & Token Manipulation Chain From One Host
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(ITDR-007 LSASS Process Handle Open By Non-System Process) OR BIOC(ITDR-007 Abnormal DACL Write To AdminSDHolder Or Privileged Group) OR BIOC(ITDR-007 Kerberos Relay To LDAP From Local Host (KrbRelayUp)) OR BIOC(ITDR-007 SeImpersonate Named-Pipe Privilege Escalation To SYSTEM) OR BIOC(ITDR-007 Access Token Theft And Impersonation Via Token Duplication) — groups credential access, ACL abuse, Kerberos relay, SeImpersonate escalation, and token theft from one host into a single Privilege Escalation incident.

Correlation CR-ITDR-0007 groups LSASS access, privileged DACL abuse, Kerberos relay, SeImpersonate escalation, and token theft from one host into a single Privilege Escalation incident.
Playbook: isolate the host, revoke the foothold account, revert the malicious DACL ACE, rotate the machine account and any exposed service-account credentials, and hunt for RBCD edits.

use_cases.name: Active Directory Privilege Escalation & Token Manipulation
use_cases.description: Detect the post-compromise local-to-domain escalation chain — LSASS credential dumping, privileged DACL abuse, Kerberos relay, SeImpersonate escalation, and access-token theft — on a domain workstation and group it into one Privilege Escalation incident.

test_cases.objective: Each escalation step fires its expected Cortex ITDR/XDR detection during SIM-ITDR-007.
preconditions: Cortex ITDR + XDR connected to the AD domain and the domain-joined workstation.
BIOCs from this card imported and enabled.
steps: Run SIM-ITDR-007 steps 1-5 against the seeded lab.
Observe the LSASS-access, DACL-write, Kerberos-relay, SeImpersonate, and token-theft detections in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: BIOC `ITDR-007 LSASS Process Handle Open By Non-System Process` fires on the credential-dump step.
BIOC `ITDR-007 Abnormal DACL Write To AdminSDHolder Or Privileged Group` fires on the bloodyAD step.
BIOC `ITDR-007 SeImpersonate Named-Pipe Privilege Escalation To SYSTEM` fires on the PrintSpoofer step.
All four XQL validation queries return >= 1 row.

test_cases.objective: The escalation steps stitch into one Privilege Escalation incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-ITDR-0007` groups the chain from one host into a single incident.

preventive_controls: Enable Credential Guard / LSA protection (RunAsPPL) so LSASS memory cannot be read by user-mode processes.
Audit and tier privileged AD objects; alert on any nTSecurityDescriptor (DACL) change to AdminSDHolder or privileged groups and review ACL grants with BloodHound.
Disable RBCD writes by non-admins and patch / monitor for Kerberos relay (KrbRelayUp) — enforce LDAP signing and channel binding.
Remove SeImpersonatePrivilege from service accounts where unnecessary and isolate IIS/MSSQL service identities.
detection_engineering: Alert on a non-system process opening a credential-read handle to lsass.exe.
Alert on 4662 directory-service writes modifying nTSecurityDescriptor on privileged objects.
Alert on a Kerberos relay from the local host to LDAP and on RBCD edits to a computer object.
Alert on a SYSTEM child spawned from a SeImpersonate service-account parent, and on access-token duplication/impersonation from a privileged process.
Correlate the escalation steps from one host into a single Privilege Escalation incident.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Initial AD privilege-escalation & token-manipulation card for SIM-ITDR-007 — LSASS dumping (T1003.001), privileged DACL abuse (T1098), Kerberos relay (T1550/T1068), SeImpersonate escalation (T1134), and access-token theft (T1134) against the itdr-module AD lab. Real BIOCs+XQL on xdr_data / ad_audit / msft_windows_security, correlation CR-ITDR-0007, GAP-11 validated/unvalidated analytics split. Wired to the adapter-gated SIM-ITDR-007 scenario (TOOL-PYPYKATZ / TOOL-BLOODYAD / TOOL-KRBRELAYUP / TOOL-PRINTSPOOFER / TOOL-TOKENVATOR).

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Causality-contract tuning. Retuned the LSASS-access, SeImpersonate-escalation, and token-theft BIOCs to surface causality-actor ownership: their field projections now carry causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_instance_id, and causality_id so the Causality Analysis Engine's CGO/actor split is traceable (the SeImpersonate BIOC keeps its actor≠causality_actor service-account tell). Paired with SIM-ITDR-007's new cgo_anchor (powershell.exe / helpdesk-admin foothold shell) and per-step causality spine — LSASS harvest → credential-reuse DACL write → same-session KrbRelayUp/PrintSpoofer escalation → Tokenvator running in PrintSpoofer's SYSTEM context (process_lineage). No dataset/ENUM/technique changes.
